text:
sarah_support: heads up — ACME's dedicated pool (pool-id: rp-acme-eu-1) started returning 429s around 09:42 UTC, sustained for ~15m. customer reports steady QPS, no obvious traffic spike.
vikram_sre: do we have x-rate-limit headers from their requests? can you paste a sample response?
sarah_support: pasted from their logs: `HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests\nDate: Tue, 12 Mar 2025 09:43:10 GMT\nX-RateLimit-Limit: 120\nX-RateLimit-Remaining: 0\nX-RateLimit-Reset: 164\nContent-Type: application/json` They said our client is sending ~110 QPS sustained.
olivia_prod: hmm, pool config shows reserved_capacity=120 qps, burst_window=10s, burst_headroom=30. If Remaining hits 0 during a bursting pattern that could still get 429s if tokens consumed by long tails.
mike_infra: can we confirm routing? maybe requests were routed to a different shard with lower headroom. checking router logs... `grep rp-acme-eu-1 /var/log/router/2025-03-12.log | tail -n 50` shows a handful of reroutes to shard-7 at 09:42:55. shard-7 had cpu/gpu load spikes.
sarah_support: customer also mentioned they use streaming responses (chunked). could sustained streaming change token accounting?
vikram_sre: yes, streaming can keep KV cache warm and increase per-request token consumption due to longer sessions. Need to check token accounting window.
olivia_prod: quick repro attempt steps for internal: 1) send 110 qps steady 1s requests for 10m to rp-acme-eu-1 2) mix 10% streaming long sessions (~512 tokens) 3) watch `admin/metrics/reserved_pool/rp-acme-eu-1` 4) inspect `quota.tokens.inflight` and per-shard buckets.
sarah_support: customer asked whether SLA should prevent this — they expect dedicated capacity to avoid 429s at their committed qps.
vikram_sre: clarify SLA: Dedicated reserves capacity but we still enforce short-term burst protections to avoid single-tenant noisy neighbors. SLA guarantees baseline throughput under normal conditions, but not unlimited burst if backing shard is saturated. We need to correlate observed shard health with their pool's reserved capacity mapping.
mike_infra: found a mismatch: pool rp-acme-eu-1 was partially pinned to shard-7 and shard-9 after last week topology change. shard-9 was drained for maintenance at 09:40 and traffic shifted to shard-7 — reduced headroom. config diff: `diff /etc/pools/rp-acme-eu-1{.old,.new}` shows `pinned_shards: [7,9]` -> `pinned_shards: [7]` during the drain, but quota recalculation lagged.
customer-rep: customer says they didn't change anything on their side — they just saw errors in production logs. They're sensitive because billing spikes when retries occur.
vikram_sre: mitigation options: 1) temporarily increase reserved capacity for rp-acme-eu-1 (+30 qps) to cover shifted load (requires infra approval) 2) enable auto-fallback to hosted-compatible model variant for excess traffic (degrades latency/quality) 3) throttle server-side client more gracefully to avoid billing churn.
olivia_prod: short-term I'd recommend option 1 + issuing a credit for retry costs. medium-term: fix quota recalculation race during shard topology changes and surface per-pool shard-health in Console.
mike_infra: I'm running a manual quota recalculation for rp-acme-eu-1 now: `./tools/poolctl recalc --pool rp-acme-eu-1 --force` — will monitor metrics.
sarah_support: thanks — I'll notify the customer and offer a 24hr credit while you confirm. @vikram_sre I'll need wording for SLA clarification.
vikram_sre: draft: "Dedicated pools reserve capacity aligned to committed QPS. During infrastructure reconfiguration (e.g., shard drains) there can be transient reductions in available headroom while quotas are reconciled; we aim to minimize these windows and will credit affected usage." happy to refine.
customer-rep: customer accepted the temporary credit offer and asked for a postmortem and steps to avoid this in future.
mike_infra: recalc finished at 09:57 UTC; metrics show `quota.remaining` stabilized and 429s dropped. I'll schedule a runbook to avoid race windows and add a pre-drain handoff to shift pools proactively.
olivia_prod: filing a follow-up: create an internal ticket to add per-pool `pinned_shards` health check and a Console alert if pool_headroom < 10% for >2m.
sarah_support: closing loop with customer now, will attach mitigation notes and timeline. thanks all :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: deployment check OK — no config mismatches detected after recalc.
vikram_sre: follow-ups: (1) postmortem draft (2) billing review for retry-induced units (3) automation to temporarily redirect pool to alternative shards during maintenance. I'll own 1 & 3.
sarah_support: noted. ending thread.
